summary: Depth-first rabbithole dossier for clusterTime; source-anchored research pack.

facts.text: [medium] ClusterTime is incremented only when there is a write to a primary node's replication operation log (oplog), and every write or event that changes state is assigned a time when applied to the primary. Sources: https://mongodb.com/blog/post/casual-guarantees-anything-casual, http://muratbuffalo.blogspot.com/2024/04/implementation-of-cluster-wide-logical.html

[medium] Cluster nodes (mongod, mongos, config server, clients) always track and include the greatest known ClusterTime when sending a message, a process called gossipping the cluster time. Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/specifications/master/source/causal-consistency/causal-consistency.md, http://muratbuffalo.blogspot.com/2024/04/implementation-of-cluster-wide-logical.html

[low] When a driver sends a non-SDAM command to a server, it MUST include the highest seen cluster time in a top-level field called $clusterTime, sending the greater of the clusterTime values from MongoClient and ClientSession. Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/specifications/master/source/sessions/driver-sessions.md

[low] A driver detects that it MUST participate in gossipping the cluster time when it sees a $clusterTime in a response received from a server, and if the new clusterTime is greater than the session's current clusterTime, the session's clusterTime MUST be advanced. Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/specifications/master/source/sessions/driver-sessions.md

[low] Cluster time is only used in replica sets and sharded clusters, and when connected to a deployment that does not support cluster times, messages sent to the server should not include $clusterTime. Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/specifications/master/source/causal-consistency/causal-consistency.md

[low] When connected to a deployment that does support cluster times, messages sent to the server should include $clusterTime, and the server reports its view of the current cluster time in the $clusterTime field in responses from the server. Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/specifications/master/source/causal-consistency/causal-consistency.md

[low] A driver MUST NOT use the clusterTime of a ClientSession anywhere else except when executing an operation with this session. Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/specifications/master/source/sessions/driver-sessions.md

[low] There is no need to do session_b.advance_cluster_time(session_a.cluster_time) because the MongoClient already gossips the highest $clusterTime seen across all client sessions, but this automatic gossiping is not true for client sessions from different MongoClients. Sources: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/DRIVERS-2860

[high] The advanceClusterTime method updates the cluster time tracked by the session with parameters for clusterTime and signature, but MUST NOT advance the clusterTime in MongoClient because the supplied clusterTime cannot be verified as valid. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/Session.md, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/specifications/master/source/sessions/driver-sessions.md

Fact 50 states "Max has been called on to help in three (3) separate instances," which is unrelated to clusterTime and appears to be noise or an error in the source data. Sources: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/DRIVERS-2860

[high] MongoDB implements causal consistency using a hybrid logical clock based on the Lamport logical clock, called clusterTime, to partially order events across replica sets and sharded clusters. Sources: https://mongodb.com/blog/post/casual-guarantees-anything-casual, https://emptysqua.re/blog/how-to-use-mongodb-causal-consistency/, https://dev.to/franckpachot/read-your-writes-on-replicas-postgresql-wait-for-lsn-and-mongodb-causal-consistency-4he2, https://vkontech.com/causal-consistency-guarantees-in-mongodb-lamport-clock-cluster-time-operation-time-and-causally-consistent-sessions/

[low] ClusterTime is represented by a <Time><Increment> pair where <Time> is a 32-bit count of seconds since the Unix epoch and <Increment> is a 32-bit integer to distinguish writes within the same second. Sources: http://muratbuffalo.blogspot.com/2024/04/implementation-of-cluster-wide-logical.html

[medium] ClusterTime is digitally signed using HMAC-SHA1 to prevent malicious clients from propagating invalid cluster times, with signing performed as a range of time for performance optimization. Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/specifications/master/source/causal-consistency/causal-consistency.md, http://muratbuffalo.blogspot.com/2024/04/implementation-of-cluster-wide-logical.html

[medium] ClusterTime values can be read by any node, but only MongoDB processes can sign new values, and the signature field does not participate in the comparison of cluster times. Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/specifications/master/source/sessions/driver-sessions.md, http://muratbuffalo.blogspot.com/2024/04/implementation-of-cluster-wide-logical.html

[low] Drivers MUST NOT gossip cluster time on SDAM commands, and the clusterTime in MongoClient should only be advanced with a $clusterTime received directly from a server, not via advanceClusterTime. Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/specifications/master/source/sessions/driver-sessions.md

[low] Two cluster times are compared using only the BsonTimestamp value of the clusterTime embedded field, including both the timestamp and the increment, while the signature field does not participate in the comparison. Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/specifications/master/source/sessions/driver-sessions.md

[high] The session's clusterTime property returns the most recent cluster time seen by the session, which is null if no operations have been executed unless advanceClusterTime has been called. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/Session.md, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/specifications/master/source/sessions/driver-sessions.md

[low] The counter from before is pretty much replaced with clusterTime, and the clusterTime at the time of the operation, returned to the Client, is called operationTime. Sources: https://vkontech.com/causal-consistency-guarantees-in-mongodb-lamport-clock-cluster-time-operation-time-and-causally-consistent-sessions/

[low] Need to clear the cache to avoid signing the data with the replica set keys that are being discarded, and the protocol must ensure that the clusterTime clients got is signed by the config server. Sources: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-30977
